summary: Hike-in, seasonally staffed lookout in Idaho's Frank Church Wilderness; the current cab dates to 1976, and sources disagree on the earlier build dates.

access.note: Hike-in only, in the Frank Church wilderness, at an active staffed lookout. No source says whether visitors may enter the cab.

corrections.why: The summit held a log cabin in the 1920s and an L-4 cab in 1934 or 1957, so 1976 replaced an older structure rather than being the first build.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The first structure is dated 1925 (firelookout.com) or the late 1920s (UIdaho file). The L-4 cab is dated 1934 by firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts, while the NHLR puts an L-4 ground house in 1957. The story reports both and does not pick one.
The NHLR gives 8,421 ft (2,567 m), which the record uses. firelookout.com and the UIdaho file give 8486 ft. The story notes the spread.
The NHLR calls the current cab a CL-100 14x14. Keeping Watch calls the cabin an R-6 15x15. Not resolved; both are reported.

The NHLR says the lookout is in full-time use. firelookout.com and Keeping Watch describe summer or peak-season staffing. The seasonal description is used because two sources agree and the NHLR wording is general.

notes_for_editor: Build dates conflict across sources: NHLR places an L-4 ground house in 1957 while firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and Keeping Watch give 1934; the first log structure is dated 1925 or the late 1920s. Design conflicts (NHLR CL-100 14x14 vs Keeping Watch R-6 15x15) and elevation conflicts (8,421 ft vs 8,486 ft) are reported, not resolved. The access level 'restricted' is an inference from hike-in, active staffed use; no source states a visitor policy for the cab. Staffing as_of 2025 is the Idaho Fire Lookouts article date (July 12, 2025); its named staff list ends in 2024. No source read records a fire this lookout spotted or one that damaged it; the Keeping Watch interview describes burned forest in view and early fires in the wider area. The 1954 yellow-paint episode is in the UIdaho file and is not a fire. The Try Ranger trail page was not read, so no trail length is given. The record's kind 'ground' was not checked against the cab-on-stone-base description.
